name: cereal
workload: 1,000,000 serialize-deserialize operations (repeated 50 times) on a shared struct, comparing total wall time across serializer libraries
claimed_speedup: 1052.46 ms vs Protobuf 2312.78 ms and Msgpack 2560.6 ms (derived from page data, ~2.2x faster than Protobuf, ~2.4x faster than Msgpack)
tradeoffs: Header-only, macro-driven intrusive/non-intrusive serialize() methods; not a schema/IDL language like Protobuf so no cross-language codegen; text/binary/XML archives supported but binary archive is what was benchmarked.
caveats: Benchmark uses old library versions (Protobuf 3.7.0, Cereal 1.2.2, Ubuntu 16.04, unspecified compiler) so absolute numbers are dated; relative ordering (cereal beating protobuf/msgpack) is the useful signal, not the exact ms figures. Compiler and optimization flags for the specific run were not stated in the README, only that Clang and GCC were both supported.
found_via: vcpkg port 'cereal' and conan-center recipe 'cereal' confirmed present; cross-referenced against community shootout github.com/thekvs/cpp-serializers (query: vcpkg conan fast serialization protobuf msgpack alternative)

name: Boost.Serialization
workload: 1,000,000 serialize-deserialize operations (repeated 50 times) on a shared struct, comparing total wall time across serializer libraries
claimed_speedup: 1195.04 ms vs Protobuf 2312.78 ms and Msgpack 2560.6 ms (derived from page data, ~1.9x faster than Protobuf, ~2.1x faster than Msgpack)
stars_or_usage: part of Boost; boostorg/serialization repo has 135 stars (mirror; usage vastly larger via Boost distribution)
tradeoffs: General-purpose C++ object graph serialization (pointers, polymorphism, versioning) rather than a schema/IDL binary format; no cross-language interchange; heavier compile-time cost than lightweight header-only competitors.
caveats: Same aged benchmark as cereal entry above (Ubuntu 16.04, unstated compiler/flags for this specific run); Boost.Serialization is not marketed as a 'fast' library, this is an incidental win in a third-party shootout, not a first-party performance claim.

name: Apache Thrift (binary protocol)
workload: 1,000,000 serialize-deserialize operations (repeated 50 times) on a shared struct, comparing total wall time across serializer libraries
claimed_speedup: 1190.22 ms (Thrift-binary) vs Msgpack 2560.6 ms (derived from page data, ~2.2x faster than Msgpack); did not beat Protobuf's 2312.78ms by as wide a margin but still faster (~1.9x)
tradeoffs: Requires IDL + code generation (thrift compiler) and an RPC framework dependency footprint; Thrift-compact variant was much slower (3474ms) than Thrift-binary in the same run, so only the binary protocol qualifies.
caveats: Same aged benchmark (Thrift 0.12.0, Ubuntu 16.04, unstated compiler/flags for this run) as the other two entries in this batch; Thrift is itself a major incumbent RPC/serialization stack, not a niche challenger, so this is a narrower/weaker claim than a purpose-built fast serializer.
